newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Southern hopeful CEPA deal will go forward.
newsitem.headline: Southern hopeful CEPA deal will go forward.

text.p: Southern Co unit Southern Electric International said on Thursday it was hopeful that an agreement to acquire a majority stake in Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) would go forward.

"I don't want to comment on the specifics of what is done and what is not done at this point but we are very hopeful that it goes forward," said Ray Harris, Southern Electric regional director in Hong Kong.
Hopewell Holdings Ltd agreed earlier this month to sell a major part of its CEPA stake to Southern Electric.

CEPA said on Thursday it had been approached by a third party about a possible acquisition of a controlling interest in the company. It said no offer or formal proposal has been received from the third party.
"Right now we are not commenting on it one way or the other because there is not a formal proposal on the table from any other source from our understanding," said Harris.

He said the company would make an announcement if one was necessary. "I can't predict what the future holds here but if there is a need for us to put out an announcement later we will do so but right now we don't see the need to do so."
Hopewell and CEPA officials were not immediately available for comment.
CEPA shares were up HK$0.10 at HK$17.95 and Hopewell was unchanged at HK$5.45.
